newsitem.title: USA: Treasury auction sidelines U.S. corp bond issuance.
newsitem.headline: Treasury auction sidelines U.S. corp bond issuance.

text.p: New issuance of U.S. corporate bonds was expected to continue to be slow on Wednesday as companies waited out the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding this week, dealers said.
"New Treasury supply makes it tougher to issue corporate bonds," said one high-grade syndicate source. "(Corporations) like to have a clearer picture of their benchmarks before pricing debt."
The Treasury plans to sell $12.0 billion of 10-year notes Wednesday and $10.0 billion of 30-year bonds Thursday. It auctioned $17.75 billion of three-year notes Tuesday.
Despite the current lull, several corporations are preparing to sell new bond issues once the auctions are over, syndicate sources say.
Later this week, Cummins Engine Co Inc is expected to sell $120 million in 30-year bonds, puttable in 10 years, via Goldman, Sachs & Co, market sources said.
Rumors continue to circulate of a possible Ford Motor $1.0 billion global 10-year debt offering via Merrill Lynch, syndicate sources said.
Also rumored is a five-year debt deal from Kellogg Co, sources said.
CIBC Woody Gundy Securities Corp will underwrite the deal, they added.
On the calendar for next week, TCI Satellite Entertainment is expected to debut in the junk market with a $350 million offering via Merrill Lynch & Co and DLJ, sources said.

Price talk on the $150 million tranche of 10-year senior subordinated notes is 10.75 percent to 11 percent, sources said. Price talk on the $200 million tranche of 10-year senior subordinated discount notes is 11.75 percent to 12 percent, sources say.
TCI Satellite, a digital broadcast satellite service company, was spun off from Tele-Communications Inc last year.
